beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: A few weeks on. Dave's back, a little more settled than last time.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I want to look back at the leap I took. And there's something new, too — a chance to go into business with someone, using something I've been quietly building. I don't know if I should take it."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for how the leap looks now.

options.text: One cycle ended the moment you jumped — this is the start of the next.
It means the leap is already over and done with.
It means you should have waited longer to jump.

elaboration: The Fool doesn't close the book once the leap happens — it just marks where one cycle ended and the next one, quietly, already began.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. Now the thing that's actually in front of me."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for what's in front of you now.

options.text: A real choice ahead — worth weighing from every angle.
It means you're going to lose someone over this.
This card just means you shouldn't trust them.

elaboration: The Lovers isn't a verdict on the outcome — it's just naming that a real decision, not a formality, is sitting in front of you.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "There's someone I'd be going into business with. I don't want to drag them into something that fails."

options.text: Choose with more than logic — trust your gut too.
Then don't drag them into it at all.

elaboration: Weighing every angle includes the ones that don't show up on a spreadsheet — this card wants your gut in the room too, not just the plan.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. I think the leap already answered half of this — I just needed to see it. Thanks. Let me sit with the rest."
